page: JWT Auth Middleware for token verification using secret key. Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {jwt} from 'hono/jwt', type {JwtVariables} from 'hono/jwt'. Verifies JWT tokens from Authorization header or cookie. HTTP header: Authorization with scheme required (Bearer, Basic). Access payload: c.get('jwtPayload'). Algorithms: HS256, HS384, HS512, RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, EdDSA. Supports both symmetric (HS*) and asymmetric (RS*, PS*, ES*, EdDSA). Optional verification: iss (issuer), aud (audience), nbf, iat, exp (default all true). Type: JwtVariables for payload typing. Options: secret (required, string), alg (required, algorithm string), cookie (optional, cookie name), headerName (optional, default 'Authorization', example 'x-custom-auth-header'), realm (optional, default request URL, WWW-Authenticate), verification (optional, VerifyOptions). Environment variable support via async middleware pattern. Questions: How to verify JWTs? Which algorithms are supported? How to access payload? Can I use custom headers? How to verify claims? How to type variables?

JWT Auth middleware usage patterns. Pattern 1: Basic JWT. jwt({secret: 'it-is-very-secret', alg: 'HS256'}). Simple secret key verification. Pattern 2: With type checking. type Variables = JwtVariables. new Hono<{Variables: Variables}>(). Infers c.get('jwtPayload') type. Pattern 3: Get payload. const payload = c.get('jwtPayload'). Returns decoded claims like {sub, name, iat, iss}. Pattern 4: With verification options. jwt({secret, alg, verification: {iss: 'my-trusted-issuer', aud: 'my-api'}}). Validates issuer and audience. Pattern 5: Environment variables. app.use('auth/*', (c, next) => { const jwtMiddleware = jwt({secret: c.env.JWT_SECRET, alg: 'HS256'}); return jwtMiddleware(c, next); }). Load secret from environment at runtime. Questions: What's the simplest setup? How to type correctly? How to get token payload? How to verify issuer/audience? How to use env variables?

JWT Auth middleware options specification. Required: secret (string, your secret key for verification). Required: alg (string, algorithm: HS256|HS384|HS512|RS256|RS384|RS512|PS256|PS384|PS512|ES256|ES384|ES512|EdDSA). Optional: cookie (string, cookie name for token extraction instead of Authorization header). Optional: headerName (string, default 'Authorization', custom header name like 'x-custom-auth-header'). Optional: realm (string, default request URL, WWW-Authenticate challenge header realm value). Optional: verification (VerifyOptions for claim validation). VerifyOptions: iss (string | RegExp for issuer validation), aud (string | string[] | RegExp for audience), nbf (boolean, default true for not-before validation), iat (boolean, default true for issued-at validation), exp (boolean, default true for expiration validation). Questions: Which options required? What are defaults? Can I use cookies? How to verify claims? Can I customize header? What's realm for?

Environment variable support pattern. Since jwt() is middleware function, can inject runtime values like environment variables. Wrap jwt() in async middleware: app.use(path, (c, next) => {const jwtMiddleware = jwt({secret: c.env.JWT_SECRET, alg}); return jwtMiddleware(c, next);}). Allows dynamic secret loading from c.env. Useful for multiple environments (dev/prod). Questions: How to use environment variables? Why wrap jwt()? When to use this pattern? Can I switch algorithms dynamically?
